subject: DPA execution & supplier audit visibility
messages:
From: Tom Reynolds <t.reynolds@medicorp.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: DPA execution & supplier audit materials request

Soojin,

Thanks for the quick intro last week. Medicorp legal is asking us to get the DPA executed before we provision any test data. A couple of things they flagged we want to confirm:

- Full subprocessor list + any planned additions in the next 90 days.
- SOC 2 type II report (or an attestation) and the most recent pen test executive summary.
- Audit access language: our legal team needs to confirm the vendor audit window (we typically ask for a 30-day window and explicit access to evidence for a rolling 12 months).

Can you share how Redwood typically handles third-party audit requests and whether you execute via DocuSign? If you can attach SOC 2/pen-test summary and the current subprocessor register that would be ideal.

Thanks,
Tom
Tom Reynolds
Head of Procurement
Medicorp
Phone: +1 415 555 0192

Attachment: Medicorp_audit_policy.pdf (policy excerpt, 42 KB)

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Tom Reynolds <t.reynolds@medicorp.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-01T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: DPA execution & supplier audit materials request

Tom — thanks, and appreciate the clear list. Looping in Rishi (legal) and Evelyn (customer success) so we can respond on the DPA and evidence. Quick answers:

- We maintain an up-to-date subprocessor registry; I can share the current export and note any planned additions.
- We can provide our SOC 2 type II attestation and the pen test executive summary (redacted as needed).
- We do execute DPAs via DocuSign for most customers; Rishi will propose our standard language on audit windows and evidence access.

Rishi/Evelyn — can you confirm the proposed system of record for the subprocessor list & whether we can commit to a 30-day audit window + 12 month evidence retention for Medicorp?

Proposed next steps: Rishi to send a redlined DPA, we share SOC2/pen-test artifacts in a secure drive link, and then send DocuSign for signatures.

— Soojin
Soojin Lee
Account Executive, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1 650 555 0123

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Tom Reynolds <t.reynolds@medicorp.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-02T08:43:00-07:00
Subject: Re: DPA execution & supplier audit materials request

Tom/Soojin — attaching our suggested redlines to the standard Redwood DPA for Medicorp (redlines_20260702.pdf). High level:

- Subprocessors: we will provide the current registry and commit to notifying Medicorp 30 days before adding a new subprocessor that handles customer data. The registry will be provided via a secure drive link.
- Audit rights: we prefer a combination of (1) Redwood-produced compliance reports (SOC 2 Type II attestation; pen test executive summary) and (2) a vendor-led audit option where Medicorp can submit a written questionnaire and request evidence. For onsite or third-party audits we require a scope aligned to our SOC 2 controls and at least 30 days' notice.
- Evidence retention: we can commit to retaining evidence for 12 months per control, with exceptions where evidence is owned by an underlying cloud provider (we will surface that in the registry).

I attached the pen test executive summary (pen_test_exec_summary.pdf) and the redlines. The redlines include a small modification to the audit clause to limit an overly broad right for unrestricted on-site audits — we believe a hybrid approach is industry standard and reduces operational risk for both parties.

If Medicorp's legal insists on unlimited onsite audit rights, we'll need to escalate to our security & compliance lead to evaluate feasibility and insurance requirements. For typical procurement timelines, DocuSign execution is fine — we sign on Redwood's side electronically and return to you.

Attachment stubs: redlines_20260702.pdf (5 pages), pen_test_exec_summary.pdf (2 pages)

— Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.com

From: Tom Reynolds <t.reynolds@medicorp.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Medicorp Legal <legal@medicorp.com>
Date: 2026-07-03T11:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: DPA execution & supplier audit materials request

Thanks Rishi — appreciate the detail and the pen test summary. Couple of clarifications from our legal team:

1) They prefer explicit language allowing a vendor-led audit plus a third-party assessment at Medicorp's option once per 12-month period. That third-party assessment should have the ability to request evidence (copies, logs) but not to access underlying production systems directly.
2) The 30-day notice is OK, but they also want a maximum 45-day response SLA for any evidence requests.

I've attached Medicorp's audit policy excerpt for context. If you can accept the hybrid model (vendor-led + one third-party assessment per year) with the 45-day evidence response SLA, we should be able to move quickly to DocuSign.

Regards,
Tom

Attachment: Medicorp_audit_policy.pdf (already sent)

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Tom Reynolds <t.reynolds@medicorp.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-06T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: DPA execution & supplier audit materials request

Tom — after coordinating with security, we can accept the hybrid audit model: vendor-produced SOC 2 + pen test artifacts, and one third-party assessment per 12 months with evidence requests limited to copies of documents/logs (no direct production access). We will commit to a 45-day SLA for providing requested evidence where feasible.

Two small asks from our side before DocuSign:
- Please confirm the authorized signer for Medicorp on the DocuSign envelope (name & title).
- Medicorp to confirm that the third-party auditor signs RedNDA (we'll provide a standard mutual NDA for the audit engagement).

I've attached the final redlined DPA (redlined_DPA_final.pdf) reflecting these concessions and the language about the 45-day response SLA. If that looks good, we'll send a DocuSign envelope and complete execution the same day. HubSpot deal: DEAL-4721 referenced for procurement team.

Attachment stub: redlined_DPA_final.pdf (6 pages)

— Rishi
